verdict.rationale: Linear ships Loops, recurring Linear Agent workflows described in plain language that run on a schedule or in response to workspace events. Documented examples include automatically updating a launch plan and posting a Slack message when a project's target date changes, and the agent can investigate and attempt fixes on new issues before an engineer sees them. The evidence covers both recurring schedules and event triggers, not just one-off actions, but it comes only from changelog-level vendor claims. missing for 10: in-depth configuration docs for Loops (trigger options, run history, failure handling), independent or hands-on corroboration that loops run reliably unattended.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Loops are a new way for Linear Agent to take on recurring work for your team. Describe the job in plain language and then choose whether it should run on a schedule or in response to an event.
Loops are recurring agent workflows for teams. They now respond to more workspace activity, including changes to initiatives, projects, and cycles.
When a project's target date changes, a loop can automatically update the launch plan and post a Slack message explaining what changed, why, and who needs to act.
When a new issue is reported, Linear Agent can investigate and attempt a fix before it reaches an engineer, reducing the load on your team.
